name: nine games I think you should play
content:
nine games I think you should play

There’s a cute trend going around Discord servers and Bluesky of “here’s a grid of nine games I’ve played which I think you should play”. it’s cute! i like it!

unfortunately, I am a woman who feels a compulsion to explain her personal taste, and, Backloggd lists are kind of jank1. Please understand that I listened to a lot of Desert Island Discs growing up, and any time I recommend something, I feel like I’m talking to Kirsty Young.

Where possible, I've tried to include both itch.io links + Steam, for whichever capital P platform you prefer. Also, you (gamer with taste reading my blog) probably know all of these, so maybe this is more just a reminder to play these games if you haven't yet.

Faceminer

You know when you’re on a vacation, and it’s late at night, but you’re not quite ready to sleep, but you also are ON HOLIDAY and so absolutely do not want to work on your own hobby project? This is, interestingly, when I actually finish playing games.

PS: If you’d like me to finish your game, make a Mac port so I can play it on my laptop xoxo. 2

Faceminer was one of these games. The short premise is it’s an idle game where you play as a cog in a machine, completing captcha’s to help train some surveillance system, and slowly work to automate the process of training the system; all while seeing the impact you are having on the global climate.

It’s very much mid-2020s Universal Paperclips.

Now - being mid-2020s Universal Paperclips on it’s own would make this a cute novelty, but nothing more. What I love is Faceminer gets the horror that came with Universal Paperclips, and specifically the horror many of us currently feel. It manages to toe that line of “girl I really want to close the game... but also how much worse can this get”

If you set your mind to it, you can probably play & finish this over a weekend.

Lok Digital

Word games are great. I pay for Puzzmo (please stop playing NYT Games ❤️)3 and adore it. However - many of my friends aren’t native English speakers, and, recommending word games is always super trickly. Some are fine for some folks, some aren’t, but, it’s always a bit of a gamble.

LOK is a game that looks like a word game, but, plays moreso with the idea of building words in a made up language. It’s very simple to grasp once you start playing.

Personally, I really like playing this on trains or flights. There’s an iPad version I should probably buy, and, if you’re of the screen time minimizing mindset, the digital game is actually based off a paper book you can buy.

Mixolumia

My first Tetris game was this weird fuckass game called “Tetris Worlds”. They gave the Tetrominos eyes. I was about six years old when my family got a copy of it, and, I kind of didn’t really get the game apart from the Tetriminos having eyes was fun.

The first Tetris game I actually got really into was Puyo Puyo Tetris. A friend I love very much (seriously, <3) had saved up and bought a Switch for Zelda: BOTW, but, refused to buy Mario Kart 8 Deluxe because he “had it on the Wii U”. However, he did in fact own Puyo Puyo Tetris. We then played a lot of Puyo Puyo Tetris.

Then, I bought a PS4 second hand for about £120. I got this to play games with friends when they came over for game nights.

I bought said PS4 in early February 2020. I didn’t really have friends over for game nights all that much.

However, I did Tetris Effect. I’d been wanting to play it for years, after seeing the really quite cool E3 trailer. And, to the surprise of nobody that knows me, I absolutely loved it. I nearly platinumed the game (I had SS rank everywhere, and only was missing the stupid achievements that involve gaining a bunch of XP).

Mixomulia is like Tetris Effect, but it’s also Puyo, and also it’s at 45 degrees and it looks visually stunning in it’s pixel art. If you’re a person who gets easily overwhelmed (hi) and wants a game to kind of just clear your head - I cannot recommend Mixolumia enough.

Demon’s Tilt

girl... I fucking love pinball. if you too love Pinball, you should play Demon’s Tilt.

The Cat Lady

When I was a stupid teenager and just finding these things called “indie games”, a friend recommend this to me. I cannot honestly remember if I own it, if they gifted it to me, or I acquired it into my Steam account some other third way, but, I definitely do own it.

And -- yes, I had seen YouTubers play the hit indie games, and I was playing the Big Indie Games of the era, but, I cannot help but see something like this (a relatively small, indie horror game like this) as one of those times you go “oh fuck, people can make games”.

nb: I know a lot of people had this moment watching Indie Game: The Movie. Given how people discuss Indie Game: The Movie, I must view this as a positive thing.4

I’m also putting this on here as a bit of an honorary recommendation to playing games with that person, and more generally hanging out with them. They helped me a bunch in realising I was, probably, in fact, a transsexual.5

Again, a common theme in this is going to be “this is a game that means a lot to me, based on where I was in the world when I played it”. I’m not going to be out here saying “The Cat Lady made me trans” (note: if someone wants to make this into a truly awful YouTube video, go for it man) but the person who recommended it to me certainly helped me figure some things quite early, in a way I know a lot of other tgirls don’t always have the space to do.

Also, it was this or The Ship - the silly jank LAN party game - or Gone Home. One is a stereotype for “and that’s why I sought to medically transition at 13” and the other should be, but sadly isn’t.6

Sadly - I never actually finished this game, but, what I did play means a lot to me; both in what’s actually there, and, for a good reminder of where I was in my life. It’s on my todo list to play through when I’m in recovery for vaginoplasty <3.

Unbeatable

Now, given the last one of “this is where I was in the world”, this has an extraordinarily boring story. Specifically, I had been meaning to play this, and I was kind of bored in the weird few days you have after New Years and before you’re back at work.7

It’s good. It’s a good game. It’s very popular online and that’s kind of for a reason.

If you’re a person who believes strongly in “making art is cool as shit, even if the art is kinda trash and especially even if it sometimes hurts a lot” you will really like this game.

1000xResist

Similar to Unbeatable, this was a game I kept seeing friends recommend, especially on Cohost (RIP).

As for what 1000x is about - it’s about identity, grief, family, protest, police violence, and the cycles that keep these going all through the lens of speculative sci-fi about clones of a teenager immune to a plague. It’s a debut title from folks who are clearly very fucking good at making video games.

And, while I have much more to say about 1000x, I really think V, white lady living in the United Kingdom, shouldn’t be the person to give you that piece. Rather - you should read this piece, and also you should just play the video game. If you play one game from this list, and you haven’t yet played 1000x, you should play 1000x.

Sayonara Wild Hearts

I’m not beating the stereotypes.

Anyway, it’s a music-video-video-game about identity and being forced by a bunch of women on motorcycles to come to terms with the fact you’re a dyke.

Again, this is a game where if you’re reading this, you’ve probably already had this recommended to you. It’s really good! It’s also like, a few hours long, and you can absolutely finish it in an evening if you don’t care about getting the highest ranks (you shouldn’t). You also get to listen to one of my favourite albums, which is a cool bonus :3

Going Under

If you:

  • have the unfortunate knowledge of what a “Jira Epic” is
  • like roguelites that play a little loose and focus more on the silly than fair and consistent gameplay

Then Going Under is a great game for you.

Unfortunately, without ruining some of my favourite surprises (which, I think are bits best seen blind) 8, I will have to talk about The Gameplay (ew).

Specifically - Going Under leans very heavy into chaos, and specifically the kind of chaos where the build & play style is pretty frequently changing. Weapons have pretty short durability, everything’s throwable, explosions have silly physics, etc etc.

To put it more simply - if you put your roguelikes on a scale from Binding of Isaac (it’s random, sure, but the actual gameplay mechanics are fairly well understood) to Spelunky (a death Will be your fault, but, you may not always be able to predict it) then Going Under scoots way past Spelunky and far into the fact that maybe death isn’t always your fault, but it will certainly be really funny.

A Conclusion / Honourable Mentions

In the original version of this, I put As Dusk Falls. I am still torn on whether I should include it. I wanted to stick to nine (that’s the trend!) but this is a game I think you really should play, and it is quite good.

Anyway, with that said - apologies if the writing was a bit shit in this one. This is mainly me spewing thoughts out into my Markdown editor. As I approach the end, I am slowly coming to the conclusion that some of these should probably have been their own blog posts... but I promised I’d make a blog post to some people so here we go.

1 if anyone who works on Backloggd is reading this, “unlisted” does not mean “only visible by people you follow”, it means only visible by people with the link. thanks.

2 Yes, I know Crossover/Wine/GPTK exists but it’s not got that. juice. Also if you are a friend who wants getting your game on Mac, please let me know (i love helping my friends out xoxo)

3I know this is a mostly light hearted blog post, but, please stop paying for NYT Games. The NYT are pretty horid to lots of groups, including women like me & especially so transgender kids. Given what I wrote about the game after, you can probably intuit I have some strong feelings here. If you'd like to move off NYT Games, most of Puzzmo's games are free - including their midi crossword!. Please try it out, and stop funding the NYT. Thanks <3

4that said, Fez is pretty good

5Past tense is crazy work here. I still am.

6You should play The Ship btw.

7This is sadly when I finish most games now.

8OK, I will say - the second to last fight in the game has one of the funniest weapon names I've seen in a while. Again, spoiler free, but if you're a fan of labour organizing you'll like it.
